title: Full-body tracking without suits or base stations
bottleneck: Convincing avatars need full-body pose, but inside-out cameras see only the upper body; legs and feet are inferred, often wrongly. IMU suits drift, base stations tether users to rooms, and computer-vision leg estimation fails during occlusion. Social VR with floating torsos persists because legs are unsolved.
why_it_blocks: Missing or wrong bodies break social presence and embodiment, limiting VR's promise for communication and training. Until bodies track reliably with no extra gear, avatars stay half-real.
current_state: Headset cameras plus IMU pucks give approximate full-body tracking for enthusiasts; machine-learning pose estimation improves steadily. Accurate, drift-free, gear-free full body tracking doesn't exist. Legs are frequently occluded from headset cameras, so lower-body pose is guessed, and wrong guesses break embodiment more than missing legs do.
